lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Northside Bakery | Delivery Driver | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Delivered morning wholesale orders to about 20 cafés and collected signed invoices.
- Loaded the van and checked each order against the dispatch list before leaving.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Jul 2021 - Feb 2023
- Owned the end-of-line test station for the humidity sensor and the yield reports the line leads used.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Built a solar-powered weather station on an STM32 that reports every 5 minutes over LoRa and runs 9 days without sun.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- Wrote the CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard and tested it against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, osciloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Experience is not newest-first.
items.because: Clearwater Sensors appears above the more recent Voltline role, obscuring the chronology.

items.says: The bakery role interrupts the engineering career story and takes too much space.
items.because: It appears before the engineering roles and takes two bullets, drawing attention away from technical experience.

items.says: Education appears before Experience despite several years of professional work.
items.because: It delays the section most likely to establish recent experience.

items.says: Skills should appear before Projects.
items.because: The current order delays the relevant technical toolkit.

items.says: The delivery bullet gives route size but no delivery outcome or performance measure.
items.because: Without a result, the scale does not show how well the deliveries were completed.

items.says: The review says to correct “cafØs” to “cafés” or “cafes.”
The dispatch-check bullet does not show what the check achieved.
The station and reports bullet does not say what the testing involved or what the reports enabled.
items.because: The technical work and reporting impact are difficult to judge.

items.says: The phrase about the reports’ audience is wordy and nonessential.
The fixture bullet should open the Clearwater Sensors entry.
“Update speed” does not identify which measure improved by 60%.
items.because: The figure could refer to download time, total update time, or throughput.

items.says: The test-rig bullet gives a test count but no result from running the tests.
“That ran” makes the rig sound like the actor.
The sentence assigns discovery of the failure causes to the saved data rather than the logger or your analysis.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The 8 kHz sampling rate has a 4 kHz Nyquist frequency, below the signal frequency.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make shared operations atomic or synchronize the interrupt handler and main loop.

items.says: The race-condition bullet does not say what changed in the system after the fix.
The fleet-scale rewrite and its results are also attributed to the Formula Student project.
items.because: The entries describe matching accomplishments in different contexts and periods.

items.says: The fleet phrase interrupts the action and delays the results.
The rewrite-and-results bullet should open the Voltline Robotics entry.
The rewrite bullet does not identify what changed in the firmware implementation.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what technical change produced the results.

items.says: The current-reduction bullet should open the weather-station project.
The publication and the school’s follow-on use have equal grammatical weight.
items.because: That obscures the school’s use as evidence of reach.

items.says: The opening bullet is too general to show what you contributed or achieved.
items.because: “Firmware and testing” hides the technical actions and their result.

items.says: The CAN-bus bullet says when testing happened but not what it established or changed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it worked reliably, resolved an issue, or enabled a race function.

items.says: “Before each race” emphasizes timing that adds little to the accomplishment.
The project’s fleet-scale rewrite and matching results conflict with the later Voltline claim.
items.because: The entries attribute a roughly 300-robot fleet accomplishment to different periods and contexts.

items.says: The rewrite bullet does not identify the technical change behind the results.
items.because: A reader cannot assess the technical contribution from the results alone.

items.says: The jitter and fault reductions lack a measurement period or baseline.
items.because: The comparison used to measure the reductions is unclear.

items.says: “Osciloscopes” is misspelled.
items.because: The misspelling can distract a reader in a technical skills list.
